questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: During a truck fire, always feel the doors first to see if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. Keep the doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: What shape are the placards that show hazardous materials in a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.3 materials, the floor liner should be:
questions.explanation: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials, use a tight floor liner. The liner must be made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: How fast the material must reach its destination.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are placed into one of nine classes. Each class explains the type of risks the material poses.

questions.question: If you find a cargo leak, how should you identify the leaking hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: If you find a cargo leak, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Do not touch or smell leaking materials because this can cause injury or death.

questions.question: Many products classified as poison are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous hazardous materials are also flammable.

questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's identification number appear?

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.explanation: A material's ID number must be on the shipping paper and on the packaging. It must also be on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must be in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine in cargo tanks, the driver must have an approved gas mask in the vehicle.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, keep them:
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Regulations prohibit explosive or flammable materials from being loaded in spaces with heaters.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking through a window.
In the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: When loading by hand, place breakable containers of corrosive liquid one at a time. Keep them upright. Never drop or roll the containers.

questions.question: Opening the trailer doors during a cargo fire may cause the fire to spread because it:

options.text: Changes the temperature of the trailer.
Provides more moisture to the trailer.

questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening the doors lets oxygen in, which can make the fire spread and get worse.

questions.question: If a box contains liquid containers, it must display:

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
The number of containers inside the box.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have arrows showing which way is up. These arrows tell handlers the correct direction to keep the box.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees receive training and testing?
questions.explanation: All drivers must learn about hazardous materials security risks. They must know how to spot and respond to threats. Training and testing must happen at least once every three years.

questions.question: If a driver receives a leaking package or shipment, they should:

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse any leaking packages or shipments of hazardous materials.

questions.question: If shipping papers show both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous ones may need to be:

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.

questions.explanation: When shipping papers list both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous ones must stand out. They can be listed first, highlighted in a bright color, or marked with an "X" in the "HM" column.

questions.question: If your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery, turn it off:
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine when loading or unloading a compressed gas tank, unless the engine runs the pump. If the engine does run the pump, turn it off after the transfer is complete but before you unhook the hoses.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are usually shaped like:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, it is important to know:

options.text: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to other packages.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from each radioactive package and passes through nearby packages. Rules control how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper must package, mark, and label hazardous materials. They must also provide the warning placards.

questions.question: To choose the right placard, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The type of container holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: To pick the right placard, you must know the hazard class of the materials, how much hazardous material you are shipping, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: A hazardous materials placard is shaped like a:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials must have a fire extinguisher with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials must have a fire extinguisher with a rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: Containers of hazardous materials must be:

options.text: Secured so they don't move during transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so they don't move during transport.
questions.explanation: Containers of hazardous materials must be secured so they will not fall, slide, or bounce around during transport.

questions.question: If shipping papers say "Inhalation Hazard," what placard should the shipper provide?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If the words "Inhalation Hazard" appear on the shipping paper or package, you must display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: A sign that your shipment contains hazardous materials is:

options.text: The shipper deals in fireworks or explosives.
Your last pickup was labeled hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper deals in fireworks or explosives.
questions.explanation: One sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is that the shipper works with such materials. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, pest control businesses, and dealers in explosives, munitions, or fireworks.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ away from buildings.
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. The only exception is a short stop for necessary actions like refueling.

questions.question: If your vehicle with explosives breaks down, warn other drivers by using:

options.text: Standing on the road and waving your arms.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, use reflective triangles or red electric lights to warn other drivers. Never use burning signals like flares or fuses.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: During loading and unloading of compressed gas tanks, the liquid discharge valves must be opened. At all other times, they must be closed.

questions.question: In addition to reading the manual, the best way to learn about hazardous materials transport is to:
questions.explanation: The manual gives you what you need to pass the test, but it is only the first step. Learn more by reading federal and state rules about hazardous materials transport and by taking hazardous materials training courses.
